nodes.summary: Call two natural numbers $a$ and $c$ equivalent in a union-find structure when they have the same root, where a number that is not a node is its own root. Let $U$ be a union-find structure with nodes $0, \dots, N-1$ and let $x, y < N$. The equivalence query on $x$ and $y$, which runs FIND-SET with path compression on $x$ and then on $y$, returns a union-find structure $U'$ and a boolean $b$ such that $U'$ has $N$…
nodes.title: Correctness of the union-find equivalence query

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $E$ be a list of pairs of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. For all vertices $a, b < n$, $a$ and $b$ are equivalent in the union-find structure returned by CONNECTED-COMPONENTS on $n$ and $E$ if and only if $a$ and $b$ are joined by a path in the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ whose edges are the unordered pairs $\{u, v\}$ with $(u, v)$ in $E$ and $u \ne v$.
nodes.title: Connected components computes reachability

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every list $E$ of pairs of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the union-find structure returned by CONNECTED-COMPONENTS on $n$ and $E$ has exactly $n$ nodes.
nodes.title: Connected components allocates $n$ nodes

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $E$ be a list of pairs of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $m$ be the length of $E$. Let $G$ be the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ whose edges are the unordered pairs $\{u, v\}$ with $(u, v)$ in $E$ and $u \ne v$, and let $k$ be the number of connected components of $G$. Running CONNECTED-COMPONENTS on $n$ and $E$ makes exactly $n$ MAKE-SET calls, $2m$ FIND-SET calls and…
nodes.title: Operation counts of connected components

nodes.summary: Given a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of vertices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, CONNECTED-COMPONENTS first builds the union-find structure with $n$ singleton nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ by $n$ MAKE-SET calls. It then processes the pairs $(u, v)$ of $E$ in list order: it asks whether $u$ and $v$ are equivalent using two FIND-SET calls, keeping the path compression done by the query, and if they are not equivalent…
nodes.title: Connected components via union-find

nodes.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and a node $x < |S|$, the value returned by the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$ (the compressed node array together with the root of $x$), with its cost discarded, equals the result of the Batteries path-compression auxiliary routine of FIND on $x$.
nodes.title: The cost-counted FIND auxiliary returns the uncounted result

nodes.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and a node $x < |S|$, if the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$ has cost $(t, w)$, where $t$ counts root tests and $w$ counts parent writes, then $t = w + 1$.
nodes.title: Root tests exceed parent writes by one

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure and $x < |S|$ a node. If the parent of $x$ in $S$ is $x$ itself, then the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$ has cost $(1, 0)$: one root test and no parent writes.
nodes.title: Cost of the FIND auxiliary at a root

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure and $x < |S|$ a node whose parent $y$ in $S$ differs from $x$. If $c_x$ and $c_y$ are the costs of the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$ and on $y$, then $c_x = (1, 0) + (c_y + (0, 1))$: one root test at $x$, then the run on $y$, then one parent write.
nodes.title: Cost recurrence of the FIND auxiliary at a non-root

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure, let $R$ be one more than the maximum rank of a node of $S$, and let $x < |S|$ be a node. The number of parent writes performed by the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$ (the second coordinate of its cost) is at most $R - \operatorname{rank}(x)$.
nodes.title: Parent writes are bounded by the rank gap

nodes.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ with node array $A$ and a node $x < |S|$, this is the recursive path-compression routine of FIND, paired with a cost in $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$. It charges $(1, 0)$ for testing whether $x$ is a root. If the parent $y$ of $x$ in $A$ equals $x$, it returns $A$ and the root $x$. Otherwise it runs on $y$, obtaining an array $A'$ and a root $r$, charges $(0, 1)$ for one parent…
nodes.title: Cost-counted FIND auxiliary

nodes.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and a node $x < |S|$, the value returned by the cost-counted FIND on $x$ (the compressed union-find structure together with the root of $x$), with its cost discarded, equals the result of the Batteries FIND with path compression on $x$.
nodes.title: The cost-counted FIND returns the FIND result

nodes.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and a node $x < |S|$, this runs the cost-counted FIND auxiliary on $x$, obtaining a node array $A'$, a root $r$ and a cost $(t, w)$. It returns the union-find structure with node array $A'$, together with $r$ as a node of that structure (whose size equals $|S|$), at cost $(t, w)$.
nodes.title: Cost-counted FIND

nodes.summary: For an array $A$ of union-find nodes and indices $x, y$ of $A$, the array returned by counted linking of $x$ and $y$ in $A$ is exactly the array produced by the uncounted Batteries link by rank of $x$ and $y$ in $A$.
nodes.title: Counted linking returns the linked array

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an array of union-find nodes, let $x, y$ be indices of $A$, and write $r_x$ and $r_y$ for the ranks stored at $x$ and $y$. Counted linking of $x$ and $y$ in $A$ makes $(t, p, w)$ rank tests, parent writes and rank writes, where $(t, p, w)$ is $(0, 0, 0)$ if $x = y$, is $(1, 1, 0)$ if $x \ne y$ and $r_y < r_x$, is $(2, 1, 1)$ if $x \ne y$ and $r_x = r_y$, and is $(2, 1, 0)$ otherwise, that is, if…
nodes.title: Operation counts of linking by rank

nodes.summary: Given an array $A$ of union-find nodes, each storing a parent index and a rank, and indices $x, y$ of $A$, this computation returns an array together with a count $(t, p, w)$ of rank tests $t$, parent writes $p$ and rank writes $w$. If $x = y$ it returns $A$ with count $(0, 0, 0)$. Otherwise it makes one rank test; if the rank of $y$ is less than the rank of $x$, it sets the parent of $y$ to $x$ (one parent write).…
nodes.title: Linking by rank with operation counts

nodes.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and indices $x, y$ of $S$, in the counted union of $x$ and $y$ in $S$ the total number of root tests made by its two FIND calls equals the total number of parent writes they make plus $2$.
nodes.title: The FIND phases of a union make two more root tests than parent writes

nodes.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and indices $x, y$ of $S$, the array returned by the counted union of $x$ and $y$ in $S$ equals the node array of the Batteries union of $x$ and $y$ in $S$ (union by rank with path compression).
nodes.title: Counted union returns the union's array

nodes.summary: For a union-find structure $S$ and indices $x, y$ of $S$, this computation runs counted FIND on $x$ in $S$, giving a structure $S_1$ and a root $r_x$; then counted FIND on $y$ in $S_1$, giving a structure $S_2$ and a root $r_y$; then counted linking of $r_x$ and $r_y$ in the node array of $S_2$. It returns the array produced by the linking, with cost $((a, b), (t, p, w))$, where $a$ and $b$ are the total numbers of…
nodes.title: Union by rank with operation counts

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a parent forest and let $x, y, a, b$ be vertices of $F$. Then $a$ and $b$ are equivalent in the forest obtained from $F$ by the union of $x$ and $y$ if and only if $a$ and $b$ are equivalent in $F$, or $a$ is equivalent to $x$ and $b$ is equivalent to $y$ in $F$, or $a$ is equivalent to $y$ and $b$ is equivalent to $x$ in $F$.
nodes.title: Equivalence after a union

nodes.summary: Two vertices $x$ and $y$ of a parent forest $F$ are equivalent when find returns the same root for $x$ as for $y$ in $F$.
nodes.title: Equivalent vertices of a parent forest

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure with $n$ nodes and parent map $p$, and let $x < n$. Then there is $d < n$ such that $p^d(x)$ is the root of $x$ and $p^k(x)$ is not the root of $x$ for every $k < d$.
nodes.title: The root is reached in fewer parent steps than there are nodes

nodes.summary: For every vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$, the vertex $x$ is equivalent in $F$ to the root that find returns for $x$.
nodes.title: Every vertex is equivalent to its representative

nodes.summary: For every vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$, the vertex $r$ that find returns for $x$ is a root of $F$: the parent of $r$ in $F$ is $r$ itself.
nodes.title: Find returns a root

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure with parent map $p$ (where $p(i) = i$ for $i \ge |S|$), let $x < |S|$, and let $p'$ be the parent map of the structure produced by FIND with path compression on $x$. Then for every natural number $i$, $p'(i)$ is the root of $x$ if $i = p^k(x)$ for some $k \ge 0$, and $p'(i) = p(i)$ otherwise.
nodes.title: FIND compresses exactly the original path to the root

nodes.summary: For every vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$, find returns the same root for the parent of $x$ in $F$ as for $x$.
nodes.title: Find is unchanged along a parent pointer

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a parent forest and let $x, y, z$ be vertices of $F$. If $z$ is not equivalent to $x$ in $F$, then find returns the same root for $z$ in the forest obtained from $F$ by the union of $x$ and $y$ as in $F$.
nodes.title: Union preserves the representatives of unrelated classes

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a parent forest, let $x, y, z$ be vertices of $F$, and let $F'$ be the forest obtained from $F$ by the union of $x$ and $y$. If $z$ is equivalent to $x$ in $F$, then find returns for $z$ in $F'$ the root that find returns for $y$ in $F$; otherwise find returns the same root for $z$ in $F'$ as in $F$.
nodes.title: Representatives after a union

nodes.summary: For every vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$ with depth certificate $d$, the cost that find with cost charges on $x$ is at most $d(x) + 1$.
nodes.title: The cost of find is at most the depth certificate plus one

nodes.summary: For every vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$, the cost that find with cost charges on $x$ equals $\ell(x) + 1$, where $\ell(x)$ is the path length of $x$: the number of non-root parent edges that find traverses from $x$.
nodes.title: The cost of find is the path length plus one

nodes.summary: For a vertex $x$ of a parent forest $F$, find with cost returns the root that find returns for $x$, together with the cost $\ell(x) + 1$, where $\ell(x)$ is the path length of $x$ (the number of non-root parent edges that find traverses from $x$). That is, it charges one unit for every visited vertex, including the root.
nodes.title: Find with cost

nodes.summary: For a parent forest $F$ with parent map $p$ and a vertex $x$, the root of $x$ is found by following parent pointers from $x$: it is $x$ itself if $p(x) = x$, and otherwise it is the root of $p(x)$.
nodes.title: Root of a vertex in a parent forest

nodes.summary: A parent forest on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ consists of a parent map $p$ from the vertices to themselves (a vertex $x$ with $p(x) = x$ is a root) and a depth certificate $d$ assigning a natural number to every vertex, such that every non-root edge strictly decreases the certificate: if $p(x) \ne x$, then $d(p(x)) < d(x)$.
nodes.title: Parent forest with a depth certificate

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a union-find structure on the indices $0, \dots, n-1$ with parent function $p$, let $x < n$, and let $r$ be the root of $x$ in $s$. After find with path compression is run on $x$, for every index $i < n$ the node at $i$ in the resulting array keeps its rank from $s$, and its parent is $r$ if $i = p^k(x)$ for some $k \ge 0$, and is its original parent $p(i)$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Effect of path-compressing find on each node

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a parent forest with depth certificate $d$, and let $r$ and $s$ be vertices. The linked depth certificate assigns to a vertex $z$ the number $d(z) + d(s) + 1$ if $z$ is equivalent to $r$ in $F$ (that is, $z$ and $r$ have the same root), and $d(z)$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Depth certificate after linking two roots

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a parent forest with parent map $p$, and let $r$ and $s$ be vertices. The linked parent map sends $r$ to $s$ and agrees with $p$ on every other vertex: it maps $z$ to $s$ if $z = r$, and to $p(z)$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Parent map after linking two roots

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a parent forest with parent map $p$ and depth certificate $d$, and let $r \ne s$ be two distinct roots of $F$. Linking $r$ to $s$ gives the parent forest whose parent map is the linked parent map (the parent of $r$ becomes $s$ and all other parents are unchanged) and whose depth certificate is the linked depth certificate (the certificate of every vertex equivalent to $r$ grows by $d(s) + 1$ and all…
nodes.title: Linking two roots of a parent forest

nodes.summary: For a parent forest $F$ with parent map $p$ and a vertex $x$, the path length of $x$ is the number of parent edges followed from $x$ to its root: it is $0$ if $p(x) = x$, and otherwise one more than the path length of $p(x)$.
nodes.title: Path length to the root

nodes.summary: For an array $A$ of union-find nodes, write $\rho_A(i)$ for the rank stored at index $i$ of $A$, or $0$ if $i$ is not an index of $A$. Let $x, y$ be indices of $A$ and let $A'$ be the array obtained from $A$ by the Batteries link by rank of $x$ and $y$. Then for every natural number $i$, $\rho_{A'}(i) = \rho_A(y) + 1$ if $x \ne y$, $\rho_A(x) = \rho_A(y)$ and $i = y$, and $\rho_{A'}(i) = \rho_A(i)$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Ranks after linking two nodes of an array

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure and $x$ a node of $S$, and let $S'$ be the structure returned by FIND on $x$ with path compression. For every natural number $i$, the rank of $i$ in $S'$ equals the rank of $i$ in $S$, where the rank of an index that is not a node is $0$.
nodes.title: Path compression preserves ranks

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure, write $\rho(i)$ for the rank of $i$ in $S$ ($0$ if $i$ is not a node of $S$), and let $x, y$ be nodes of $S$ such that $y$ is a root, that is, the parent of $y$ is $y$. Let $S'$ be the result of linking $x$ and $y$ by rank. Then for every natural number $i$, the rank of $i$ in $S'$ is $\rho(y) + 1$ if $x \ne y$, $\rho(x) = \rho(y)$ and $i = y$, and is $\rho(i)$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Ranks after linking in a union-find structure

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a union-find structure, write $\rho(i)$ for the rank of $i$ in $S$ ($0$ if $i$ is not a node of $S$) and $r(i)$ for the root of $i$ in $S$. For nodes $x, y$ of $S$ and every natural number $i$, the rank of $i$ in the union of $x$ and $y$ in $S$ (union by rank with path compression) is $\rho(r(y)) + 1$ if $r(x) \ne r(y)$, $\rho(r(x)) = \rho(r(y))$ and $r(y) = i$, and is $\rho(i)$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Ranks after a union

nodes.summary: Let $U$ be a union-find structure on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $x, y < n$ be roots of $U$, i.e. each is its own parent. Let $U'$ be obtained by linking $x$ and $y$ by rank: nothing changes if $x = y$; otherwise, if $\operatorname{rank}(y) < \operatorname{rank}(x)$ then $y$ gets parent $x$, and if not then $x$ gets parent $y$ and, when the two ranks are equal, the rank of $y$ increases by one. Then for every…
nodes.title: Linking two roots by rank

nodes.summary: Let $U$ be a union-find structure on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $x, y < n$. Run find with path compression on $x$ in $U$, giving a structure $U_1$ and a root $r_x$; then run find on $y$ in $U_1$ (not in $U$), giving a structure $U_2$ and a root $r_y$. Then the node array of the union of $x$ and $y$ in $U$ equals the array obtained from the node array of $U_2$ by linking $r_x$ and $r_y$ by rank: nothing changes if…
nodes.title: Union unfolds to two finds and a link

nodes.summary: If $x$ and $y$ are equivalent vertices of a parent forest $F$, then the union of $x$ and $y$ in $F$ is $F$ itself.
nodes.title: Union of equivalent vertices changes nothing

nodes.summary: For every parent forest $F$ and vertices $x$ and $y$, the vertices $x$ and $y$ are equivalent in the forest obtained from $F$ by the union of $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: Union makes its arguments equivalent

nodes.summary: For every parent forest $F$ with depth certificate $d$ and vertices $x$ and $y$, the cost charged for the union of $x$ and $y$ in $F$ (two root searches at one unit per visited vertex, plus one unit for the link when the roots differ) is at most $d(x) + d(y) + 3$.
nodes.title: Cost bound for union in a parent forest

nodes.summary: For a parent forest $F$ and vertices $x$ and $y$, the costed union returns the union of $x$ and $y$ in $F$ together with a cost equal to the cost of finding the root of $x$ plus the cost of finding the root of $y$ (each one unit per visited vertex, including the root), plus one more unit when the roots of $x$ and $y$ are distinct; when they coincide, union performs no link and none is charged.
nodes.title: Union in a parent forest with cost

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a union-find forest on $n$ vertices: each vertex $z$ has a parent $p(z)$, where roots are their own parents, and a depth certificate $d(z) \in \mathbb{N}$ with $d(p(z)) < d(z)$ whenever $p(z) \ne z$. Let $x$ and $y$ be vertices, and let $r_x$ and $r_y$ be the roots reached from $x$ and $y$ by following parent pointers. If $r_x = r_y$, the union of $x$ and $y$ in $F$ is $F$ itself. Otherwise it is the…
nodes.title: Union in a union-find forest
Computer Science

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
